correctness.rationale: For each N>=2 the exact cycle renewal equation and killed Brownian exponential Laplace bound are valid. Independent Gaussian sum/difference yields the exact E(exp(-kappa M2)) transform. At kappa=lambda/2 it equals (4/3)(1-1/sqrt7)<1; a strictly positive exponential supersolution bounds eventual first capture after monotone iteration over all finite cycles. A positive-probability first-cycle excursion transfers every x>0 to the region where this bound is below 1. The reflection principle establishes the no-reset moment cutoff, and limits as r→0 and ∞ are justified. The numerical checker independently confirms transform values but does not replace proof.

value.rationale: The result establishes a sharp structural N=1 versus N>=2 dichotomy for an experimentally motivated collective reset rule. The N>=3 finite-mean to positive-eternal-survival transition at arbitrarily weak positive reset rate is substantive, physically relevant to finite-time censoring, and proved with an all-parameter exponential upper bound on capture, rather than an arbitrary finite slice.
